question.problem:
Consider the transformation $f:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2},$ defined as

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}^{2} \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡({x}_{1}+{x}_{2})\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

If the linear approximation of $f$ at  $a=[\begin{aligned}\frac{\pi }{2} \\ \frac{\pi }{2}\end{aligned}]$ is given by

$$
f(x)≈[\begin{aligned}\frac{\pi }{2}+\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{4} \\ ∗\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 & ∗ \\ ∗ & -1\end{aligned}](x-[\begin{aligned}\frac{\pi }{2} \\ \frac{\pi }{2}\end{aligned}]),
$$

what is the sum of the missing values?

current_example.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $\boldsymbol{f}:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m$ is defined by 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14130164/assets/ce62c80229cd68cb20d75dc7e78b25fd6657be9b0b98e1c407b2a77fe20fb248.svg) 

where $f_1,f_2,\ldots,f_m$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $\boldsymbol{f}$ is differentiable at $\mathbf{x},$ then the total derivative of $\boldsymbol{f}$ at $\mathbf{x},$ denoted $\boldsymbol{f}'(\mathbf{x}),$ is given by the $m \times n$ matrix

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14130164/assets/7f632313d2f40f173e3114b1021686a81074f69fef265496abfb05bf6ef81e28.svg)

In our case, we have the following:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14130164/assets/76ad0487adff51a213a8862ade6ab29036e489b896f6ad0442b616de2b05aa79.svg)

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}({x}_{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡{x}_{1})={x}_{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡{x}_{1},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}({x}_{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡{x}_{1})=\operatorname{sin}⁡{x}_{1} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}(\operatorname{sin}⁡{x}_{2})=0,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}(\operatorname{sin}⁡{x}_{2})=\operatorname{cos}⁡{x}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14130164/assets/3df893dd59cf697c36078d409c1150f31e8d979d346293ffbd29e8b49d4b212b.svg)

Evaluating $\boldsymbol{f}$ and its derivative at ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14130164/assets/dfe2515d2311feb7fe05a6e466d80546a022247d040f7c77bb8c3aaad277f0e9.svg) we have

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14130164/assets/be94ebcdfb1dfc55ef551669ec7787761221b365cfa7ad939b53b8f536e0566c.svg)

The linear approximation of $\boldsymbol{f}$ at $\mathbf x = \mathbf a$ is given by

$$
\boldsymbol{f}\left(\mathbf x \right) \approx \boldsymbol{f}(\mathbf a) + \boldsymbol{f}'(\mathbf a)(\mathbf x - \mathbf a).
$$

Substituting $\boldsymbol{f}(\mathbf a),$ $\boldsymbol{f}'(\mathbf a),$ and $\mathbf a$ in the equation above, we obtain

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14130164/assets/5903bd932d792bec2f0830ca6b3d4eb37fb97107f65f9168bee90dd2dc252c07.svg)
